body.statement: If \(\tau_{t,\ell}=\tau_{r,\ell}\) for every \(t,r\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), then \(\theta_j(\Pi)=\tau_{t,j}\) for every \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) and every legal \(t\), reproducing Theorem \(4.1\) of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo. The extension is strict: for \(T=3\), \(p=1\), \(\mathcal S=\{000,001,011\}\), and \(\Pi=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\), the calendar-varying model yields \(\theta_0=(\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2\) and \(\theta_1=(-\tau_{2,0}+\tau_{3,0})/2+\tau_{3,1}\), so the coefficient vector is not determined by a time-homogeneous lag-effect vector outside the comparator's submodel.
body.justification: The reduction anchors the tensor to the published dynamic RIPW theorem while the three-period witness proves that retaining calendar time adds genuine identifying content.
body.gap: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo and de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille both impose time-constant distributed-lag effects for their coefficient recovery results.
body.consumer: Applied users can distinguish a valid homogeneous dynamic interpretation from calendar-specific current-effect contamination rather than silently pooling the two.
